summary: The note explains how cloud computing helps small and medium enterprises (SMEs) boost productivity, cut costs and scale. It compares cloud with on-premises and traditional IT, outlines IaaS, PaaS and SaaS, and cites case studies (TechQuickie, Bolder Designs). It closes with a forecast of 25% year-over-year cloud adoption growth among SMEs.
one_line: Cloud computing gives SMEs accessibility, cost efficiency, scalability and continuity compared with on-premises IT, supported by case studies and growth forecasts.
key_facts: A September 15, 2023 TechSME Insights report shows a significant upward trend in cloud adoption among SMEs, with evidence of increased productivity and scalability.
Johnathan Morris, CTO of InnovateSME Solutions, said cloud computing "has fundamentally changed not just how we store data but how we conduct business."
Cloud services let SMEs pay for what they use and scale up as needed, removing the need for large capital investments in IT infrastructure.
Rachel Smith, CEO of a mid-size retail chain, said on October 20, 2023 that moving to the cloud was revolutionary and gave the company agility to adapt to market demands.
Financial consultant Mike Anderson noted in a November 5, 2023 blog that cloud computing typically uses a subscription model that includes updates and maintenance in the fee.

On-premises infrastructure gives full control over data but requires the company to handle all maintenance and upgrades; cloud providers handle infrastructure, maintenance, upgrades and often security.

Isaac Green of NextGen Tech said on-premises offers peace of mind on data control at the cost of flexibility, while cloud offers elasticity and cost predictability but creates dependency on service providers.

IaaS provides virtualized computing resources like servers and storage, PaaS lets customers develop, run and manage applications without maintaining infrastructure, and SaaS delivers software over the internet by subscription.
SaaS is the most common form of cloud computing for SMEs; examples include Adobe Creative Cloud, Salesforce and Microsoft 365.
A December 1, 2023 SME Cloud Innovations Journal case study found startup TechQuickie saw a 40% increase in productivity after migrating to the cloud, according to CEO Linda Bennett.
A study of Bolder Designs, a medium-sized graphic design firm, found a 50% reduction in IT expenses after adopting cloud solutions; CIO Tom Riddle cited real-time collaboration across geographies.
Cloud computing paired with backup and disaster recovery keeps SME services running during power outages or natural disasters.
Global SME Tech Outlook 2024 forecasts cloud adoption among SMEs will grow 25% year-over-year.
